chapter_title: Chương 286: 0287 [Plants vs. Zombies Sắp Ra Mắt]

segments.title: Chương 286: 0287 [Plants vs. Zombies Sắp Ra Mắt]
segments.content:
It was the end of the year, and it was time for various annual meetings and ranking lists to be released.

Each had its own organization and way of doing things, and they all came up with various gimmicks.

For instance, the group that sold computer hardware, software, and communication equipment held the IT Fortune Annual Conference and the Chief Information Officer Annual Conference. They merged them and called it the "Two Sessions of the IT Industry."

Those in the gaming business had the Gaming Industry Annual Conference, calling it the "Golden Rooster Awards of the Gaming Industry."

Pah, how unlucky!

Chen Guiliang had to attend, because this year was extremely special. All company bosses involved in the gaming business had to come in person!

The venue was very high-end, the auditorium of the National Z-Association.

Choosing this place for the conference was not without reason.

You couldn't be early, nor could you be late; you had to time your arrival just right to line up for the security check.

Regardless of your status, you had to queue up obediently first.

Chen Guiliang was at the back of the line, slowly inching forward.

After queuing for who knows how long, Chen Guiliang turned his head and saw Pony Ma standing behind him.

"Hello," Pony Ma greeted with a smile.

Chen Guiliang nodded in acknowledgment. "Hello. The five-digit QQ numbers are very useful. I only kept one for myself and used the rest to reward my executives."

Pony Ma didn't know whether to laugh or cry, only then recalling his previous conversation with Chen Guiliang.

Pony Ma said, "Your speech from a while ago was excellent."

Is he mocking Li Yanhong here?

"Thank you," Chen Guiliang said, then changed the subject, "Are the licensing negotiations for 'Dungeon Fighter Online' still ongoing?"

Pony Ma asked, "Is Game Science planning to join the negotiations?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It's possible."

The game meant to compete with it, "Future Era," was already on its third dungeon instance.

A closed beta for a thousand players was scheduled for before the Spring Festival, mainly for stress testing.

Pony Ma said no more. He was confident he could beat the other distributors.

Chen Guiliang finally reached the security checkpoint, took off his coat, and held out his arms to undergo a thorough inspection by the security personnel.

There weren't even any reporters taking photos outside the venue; pictures could only be taken at specific times and in designated locations.

It was nothing like last year's event in Xiamen, which was a chaotic circus. They even held a singing contest for the bosses and executives of gaming companies. Ding Sanshi sang and even placed near the top; he was incredible.

Last year there were also various forums, exhibition booths could be set up, and the event lasted for several days, allowing Chinese and foreign game companies to seize the opportunity to discuss business.

This year, there was none of that, and the event was only half a day long.

Moreover, the schedule was extremely tight. By the time everyone passed through security, the opening ceremony was about to begin.

No wonder the security was so strict.

This kind of situation was unprecedented, indicating that the online gaming industry was being taken very seriously.

Faced with such a grand occasion, Chen Guiliang once again recalled Li Yanhong's speech: the gaming industry is just a small sector of the global internet...

Chen Guiliang saw Tao Chenggang from a distance. The two nodded to each other but didn't approach for a chat, instead going to their respective seats. It was much the same for others; they found their seats and sat down, at most whispering to the person next to them.

To Chen Guiliang's left sat Wang Zijie of 9you, and to his right sat Wu Hongbing of Junnet.

"You're here?" Wang Zijie said in a low voice.

Chen Guiliang said, "Morning."

Wang Zijie said, "They've really rushed things this year, compressing the whole schedule into half a day."

"Indeed," Chen Guiliang said, making small talk. "Has 'Audition Online' broken 800,000 peak concurrent users?"

Wang Zijie smiled proudly. "We broke 800,000 half a month ago."

Chen Guiliang expressed his sincere admiration. "Impressive."

Wang Zijie said, "'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' isn't bad either. It broke 500,000 six months ago."

Chen Guiliang said, "That was when public interest was at its peak. It dropped to just over 300,000 a week later. But it's bounced back now, with weekend peaks basically above 450,000."

"Then you're truly amazing," Wang Zijie praised. "A lot of 'Audition Online' players are from internet cafes, so a peak of 800,000 concurrent users is nothing. But 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' players are primarily on their own computers, so a weekend peak of 450,000 is terrifying."

The two had no direct competition, so they sat together trading compliments.

The user data for everyone's games was on the rise. Besides solid game content, it was also because China's internet was developing at lightning speed.

The number of Chinese internet users would reach 137 million by the end of the year (and a large number of internet cafe users weren't even counted). Moreover, broadband users had exceeded 100 million, and mobile internet users had reached 17 million.

During this time, while working on color ringtones, Huang Xinyuan was also vigorously developing Hainai's mobile WAP site, even making the ringtones downloadable on the WAP site.

Currently, the Hainai WAP site had reached 230,000 registered users, and mobile Weibo users had already surpassed 100,000.

Chen Guiliang glanced at Wu Hongbing, who was sitting on his other side.

The man looked back at him. They nodded at each other without speaking.

Wu Hongbing sold game point cards, and "Reign of Might" also worked with him.

Suddenly, the entire hall fell silent.

A very high-ranking official gave the opening remarks, speaking for less than five minutes.

Then came speeches from leaders of various ministries and commissions, almost all kept within five minutes. Some were only two or three minutes long.

After the leaders finished speaking, the organizers immediately presented their annual work summary.

The event's schedule was so tight it could be described as a race against time.

Once the work summary was concluded, they immediately began commending model local governments, outstanding industry bases, outstanding gaming media, outstanding industry self-discipline units...

Next came the main event: the release of the China Game Ranking System!

This was not some game chart, but more like a whitelist system for the gaming industry.

It was endorsed by multiple national ministries, including Information Industry, Culture, Science and Technology, Education, and Taxation, and its design was led by the CGIA (China Game Software Association). It covered four major dimensions: game products, enterprise qualifications, auxiliary services (media and channels), and individual contributions.

For example, a game would lose points for not implementing anti-addiction warnings. Tax evasion would also result in a deduction of points. Inappropriate words or actions by a gaming company's boss would also lead to a deduction.

There were also many ways to earn points, such as exporting games overseas, innovating game models, and so on.

Wang Zijie listened with a wry smile. "If you lose too many points, what's the penalty?"

Chen Guiliang thought to himself: This is laying the groundwork for game registration numbers!

In the future, online games would implement a registration number system. Companies with scores that were too low would definitely be throttled.

This whitelist was like a teacher taking attendance, while the game registration number was like the final exam. If you never showed up for roll call, did you really expect to pass the final?

At this point in the event, most of the leaders began to leave.

The atmosphere in the hall instantly relaxed, just like when the head teacher leaves the classroom.

The next 70 minutes were for speeches by the bosses of the game companies.

Each person was limited to 3 minutes.

And while one was speaking, the next person had to be getting ready in advance.

The time was being managed so damn tightly.

The bosses who were fond of long-winded, rambling speeches were clearly not used to this arrangement. They read from their scripts awkwardly.

Chen Guiliang had also prepared a script, but he didn't take it out.

"To keep it short, I'm Chen Guiliang from Game Science."

Chen Guiliang said, "This year's theme is innovation, creativity, and creation. 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' is a secondary innovation based on 'BANG!', and Youfutong is also an innovation on top of payment 1.0. Innovating on the shoulders of giants is still innovation, but I hope my esteemed colleagues will not simply copy. While queuing for security just now, I chatted a bit with Tencent's Boss Ma. His 'Heroes of Killing' and 'QQ Farm' are quite well done..."

"Hahahaha!"

The whole audience roared with laughter.

Pony Ma remained expressionless.

Chen Guiliang added, "If Boss Ma gives me another 10 five-digit QQ numbers, I'm willing to take back what I just said."

The room burst into laughter again.

The atmosphere today had been quite dull, and it was rare to have someone willing to joke around. Everyone present was very appreciative.

This seemed to be the first time there had been collective laughter all day, and it happened twice in a row.

Pony Ma smiled too.

Chen Guiliang said, "Next, Game Science will be launching two games. One is 'Plants vs. Zombies,' set for release on January 1st. It can be played online or as a standalone game. The other is 'Future Era,' which will begin closed beta testing before the Spring Festival, with only 1,000 beta accounts available. The data will be wiped after the beta test ends. We hope you all look forward to them. Thank you!"

He finished his speech and left the stage, and the next person went up.

But the game company bosses in attendance felt a certain pressure.

What the hell was this about releasing two new games in a row within a short span of a month and a half?

Since launching "Legends of the Three Kingdoms," Game Science had only made a few small games like "Happy Farm." Now they were suddenly putting out two?

If it were anyone else saying this, no one would have taken it seriously.

But Tao Chenggang had publicly stated multiple times that "Reign of Might" had accepted a lot of advice from Chen Guiliang. Who would dare to underestimate him?

Chen Guiliang returned to his seat, and Wang Zijie immediately asked, "'Future Era' is an MMO?"

"You could say that," Chen Guiliang said ambiguously.

Wu Hongbing, from the other side, chimed in, "Do you need Junnet to help you sell point cards?"

Chen Guiliang said, "We can cooperate."

Although his Youfutong could also be used for top-ups, its offline channels were not fully established, whereas Junnet had very mature channels in internet cafes, newsstands, and convenience stores.

Wu Hongbing, who hadn't spoken to Chen Guiliang until now, instantly became proactive upon hearing this, taking out his phone and saying, "President Chen, let's exchange contact information."

Chen Guiliang also took out his phone.

After saving the contact, Wu Hongbing said, "Let's keep in touch. Our companies are close to each other, close enough to walk over for a visit. Junnet welcomes President Chen anytime."

"I'll have to rely on President Wu's help to sell top-up cards," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

With a shared interest, the two quickly became friends.

After the industry representatives' speeches concluded, the award ceremony began immediately.

The awards were also rushed.

There were 25 award categories, with 10 winners for each. A total of 250 people would go on stage to receive awards, but it all had to be done within half an hour.

Chen Guiliang went up on stage several times.

Ding Sanshi was the busiest, winning a full 10 awards!

Tao Chenggang and Shi Yuzhu both won the 2006 Rising Star in Gaming award.

Chen Guiliang, on the other hand, received the Person of the Year award.

Wu Hongbing, the point card seller sitting next to him, was also surprisingly a Person of the Year.

Chen Guiliang also received a bunch of awards like Best Green Game of the Year, Best Casual Game, Best Domestic Online Game, Best Art Design...

This year, the Best Mobile Game award appeared for the first time.

Chen Tianqiao actually won this award, because "The World of Legend" had released a mobile version.

After the award ceremony, everyone lined up to leave the venue.

It wasn't until they were out on the street that Wang Zijie complained, "That was suffocating. First time I've ever encountered an event scheduled like this."

Chen Guiliang said, "The stuffiness I don't mind. But compressing a three-day event into half a day is bound to make people tense."

Tao Chenggang called him. "Let's have dinner tonight. Invite all the other bosses you know, see if they'll come."

"Okay," Chen Guiliang said.

That night was another gathering with a lot of drinking, the details of which will be omitted.

In the following day's media reports, although the focus was on the whitelist and the awards, what readers were most interested in were Chen Guiliang's two new games.

The news had been leaked six months ago, and now they were finally about to be released.

Chen Guiliang and "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" both had die-hard fans. They flocked to the Game Science Interactive Entertainment platform and discovered that "Plants vs. Zombies" was already available for pre-order.

The price was 5 yuan...

Is it really a standalone game????

And it's being sold so cheap!

That was the price of a pirated game CD from a street stall.

In mainland China, standalone games had always sold dismally.

"Plants vs. Zombies" was too cheap; it was bound to lose money.

Many users of the Game Science platform had already topped up their accounts before. Seeing they still had a balance, they went ahead and pre-ordered a copy.

On the first day of pre-orders, more than 200 copies were sold.

On the second day, more than 300 copies.

On the third day, over 500 copies were sold...

They were all waiting for New Year's Day to download it and see just what kind of oddity Chen Guiliang had created.
